title: Optimized minimal genome-wide human sgRNA library
model: K562 cells, genome-wide Brunello knockout library (77,441 guides) — benchmark arm of a minimal-library methods paper
contrast: Day 24 vs day 0 proliferation dropout (2 vs 2)
paper_method: Library benchmarking against reference essential-gene sets (no per-gene hit table)
paper_calls: No biological hit table; the paper reports core-essential-gene recovery as a performance metric
barcs_calls: 968 genes at FDR 0.10 (842 depleted); no usable control null (the Brunello NO_CURRENT non-targeting guides were cloned at near-zero depth here, ~90 total reads at day 0)
named_hits: Core-essential positive controls all strongly depleted at FDR 0.10 (NOP58 #2, RPTOR #3, POLR3B #5, CCT7 #10, RPL3, RPS19, POLR2A, POLR2B, PSMA1, CDK1, MYC)
verdict: A proliferation benchmark screen; BARCS recovers essential-gene dropout correctly (phosphatase, nucleolar, chaperonin, RNA-pol and ribosome genes dominate the depleted list), but the deposited library has no usable non-targeting controls so the hit list cannot be calibrated.
